sanity_expectations: For any fixed m and g, a is exactly 0 throughout the central sticking region |F| <= (mu_s + eta*log(1 + m*g/N0))*m*g.

The width of the zero-acceleration region increases with normal load m*g because eta>0, so at the same normalized force ratio near mu_s a heavier or higher-g case can remain stuck while a lighter or lower-g case slides.
For fixed m and g in the sliding regime, a has the same sign as F and is approximately antisymmetric: a(-F,m,g) = -a(F,m,g).

For fixed m and g above breakaway, a(F,m,g) is not exactly affine in F; its incremental growth with |F| changes across the sliding branch because the opposing friction term weakens saturatingly rather than remaining constant.

At matched excess ratio above breakaway, changing load ratio m*g/N0 changes the mid-range sliding curvature because delta=0.5 modulates the effective exponential rate; the difference is strongest at moderate suprathreshold loads and weakens in the stuck limit and deep saturation limit.
Increasing g at fixed F and m can switch a trial from sliding to sticking near threshold, and when both trials slide, larger g generally reduces |a| by increasing frictional resistance.

Because freedom_change is none and g was explicitly declared as a varied V input in this record, preserve F, m, and g as sampled axes. Parameter choices are physically admissible and avoid the parent-recovery limits: eta>0 makes the static threshold depend measurably on normal load m*g; delta=0.5 with the provided constraint delta>-1 makes the suprathreshold exponential rate increase with load through 1+delta*log(1+m*g/N0), remaining positive over the chosen g,m ranges; beta=2 and gamma=3 give visible but not instant saturation of the sliding-friction weakening. The chosen ranges expose the recorded mechanisms. With m in 0.5-5 kg and g in 3-20 m/s^2, normal load m*g spans 1.5-100 N, so log(1+m*g/N0) varies substantially and both the load-dependent breakaway threshold and the load-dependent sliding-branch curvature are active. F in -30 to 30 N crosses zero and sweeps from subthreshold sticking into moderate and strong sliding for light and heavy loads without putting essentially all cases deep into saturation. Near threshold, different (m,g) at similar force ratio |F|/(m*g) can fall on different sides of stick-slip onset because of the eta*log(1+m*g/N0) term. Above threshold, the same excess ratio at different loads gives different acceleration curvature because delta couples load ratio into the effective weakening rate. Some high-load combinations within the F range will remain stuck over a broader central force window; that is intended because the branch transition itself is diagnostically important. No observation noise is added.
